tldr: This paper presents a quantum algorithm with provable exponential speedup for computing persistence in topological data analysis, a problem of practical interest.
motivation: Topological data analysis (TDA) is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive. The authors aim to provide a quantum algorithm with provable speedup, potentially enabling practical applications.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm for computing persistence in TDA, likely leveraging quantum linear algebra and sampling techniques to achieve exponential speedup over classical methods.
result: The paper proves a quantum speedup for computing persistence, demonstrating a clear advantage over classical algorithms for this problem.
conclusion: The work provides a significant theoretical contribution to quantum algorithms for data analysis, with potential practical implications for quantum computing applications.

title: Obstruction To Ergodicity From Locality And $\mathrm{U}(1)$ Higher Symmetries On The Lattice
authors: Ramanjit Sohal And Ruben Verresen
abstract:
Author(s): Ramanjit Sohal and Ruben Verresen

We argue that the presence of any exact U(1) higher-form symmetry, under mild assumptions, presents a fundamental obstruction to ergodicity under unitary dynamics in lattice systems with local interactions and finite on-site Hilbert space dimension. Focusing on the two-dimensional case, we show that…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060401] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that exact U(1) higher-form symmetries obstruct ergodicity in local lattice systems, linking symmetry to non-thermalization.
motivation: Understanding when quantum systems fail to thermalize is fundamental; higher-form symmetries are a novel ingredient that may prevent ergodicity.
method: The authors use rigorous arguments based on locality and the presence of exact U(1) higher-form symmetries to show that certain conserved quantities prevent ergodicity under unitary dynamics.
result: They demonstrate that in two-dimensional lattice systems with finite on-site Hilbert space, any exact U(1) higher-form symmetry leads to a fundamental obstruction to ergodicity.
conclusion: This establishes a new mechanism for non-ergodicity, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.

title: Single-Period Floquet Control Of Bosonic Codes With Quantum Lattice Gates
authors: Tangyou Huang, Lei Du, And Lingzhen Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Tangyou Huang, Lei Du, and Lingzhen Guo

Bosonic codes constitute a promising route to fault-tolerant quantum computing. Existing Floquet protocols enable analytical construction of bosonic codes but typically rely on slow adiabatic ramps with thousands of driving periods. In this Letter, we circumvent this bottleneck by introducing an ana…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060602] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces an analytical single-period Floquet protocol for constructing bosonic codes, avoiding slow adiabatic ramps and enabling fast, fault-tolerant quantum computing.
motivation: Existing Floquet protocols for bosonic codes require thousands of driving periods due to adiabatic ramps, which is inefficient. The authors aim to circumvent this bottleneck by designing a single-period protocol.
method: The authors propose an analytical construction of a single-period Floquet drive using quantum lattice gates, which directly generates the desired bosonic code without adiabatic evolution.
result: The protocol achieves fast and accurate code generation, significantly reducing the number of driving periods compared to previous methods, and is validated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient approach to bosonic code construction, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing with Floquet engineering.

title: Decoy-State Quantum Key Distribution Over 227 Km With A Frequency-Converted Telecom Single-Photon Source
authors: Frederik Brooke Barnes, Roberto G. Pousa, Christopher L. Morrison, Zhe Xian Koong, Joseph Ho, Francesco Graffitti, John Jeffers, Daniel K. L. Oi, Brian D. Gerardot, And Alessandro Fedrizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Frederik Brooke Barnes, Roberto G. Pousa, Christopher L. Morrison, Zhe Xian Koong, Joseph Ho, Francesco Graffitti, John Jeffers, Daniel K. L. Oi, Brian D. Gerardot, and Alessandro Fedrizzi

We implement a decoy-state quantum key distribution scheme using a telecom C-band single-emitter source. The decoy states are created by varying the optical excitation of the quantum emitter to modulate the photon-number distribution. We provide an analysis of our scheme based on existing security p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060801] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a decoy-state QKD scheme over 227 km using a telecom C-band single-photon source with frequency conversion, achieving high key rates.
motivation: To enable practical long-distance QKD with a single-photon source, which is crucial for quantum networks, by overcoming the limitations of attenuated laser sources.
method: The authors implement decoy-state QKD by varying the optical excitation of a quantum emitter to modulate the photon-number distribution, and use frequency conversion to telecom C-band. They analyze the scheme using existing security proofs.
result: They achieve a secure key rate over 227 km of fiber, demonstrating the viability of single-emitter sources for long-distance QKD.
conclusion: The work shows that quantum emitter-based sources can be used for practical QKD, advancing the development of quantum networks.

title: Restriction-based Certificate Of Bipartite Schmidt Rank In Hypergraph States
authors: C. Fajardo And M. Paraschiv
abstract:
Author(s): C. Fajardo and M. Paraschiv

We investigate bipartite entanglement in qubit hypergraph states across an arbitrary fixed bipartition. Using the real equally weighted representation, the Schmidt rank across the cut can be computed as the real rank of a phase-cleaned cross-cut sign matrix. Whereas graph states admit an exact cut-r…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022410] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates bipartite entanglement in hypergraph states, providing a method to compute Schmidt rank across a bipartition using real equally weighted representation.
motivation: Understanding entanglement in hypergraph states is important for quantum information processing, and existing methods for graph states do not directly apply to hypergraph states.
method: The authors use the real equally weighted representation and define a phase-cleaned cross-cut sign matrix, whose real rank gives the Schmidt rank for the bipartition.
result: They provide a certificate for the Schmidt rank in hypergraph states, extending results from graph states to hypergraph states.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of entanglement in hypergraph states, offering a practical tool for quantifying bipartite entanglement in these states.

title: Pulsed Generation Of Continuous-variable Cluster States In A Phononic Quantum Network
authors: Anuvetha Govindarajan, Mitch Mazzei, Hailin Wang, And Lin Tian
abstract:
Author(s): Anuvetha Govindarajan, Mitch Mazzei, Hailin Wang, and Lin Tian

Cluster states are multipartite entangled states that are maximally connected and resilient to decoherence, making them valuable resources for quantum information processing. Continuous-variable (CV) cluster states have been extensively investigated for such applications. Here we present a pulsed pr…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023505] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a pulsed scheme to generate continuous-variable cluster states in a phononic quantum network, leveraging hybrid quantum systems for scalable quantum information processing.
motivation: Continuous-variable cluster states are valuable for quantum information processing, but their generation in scalable platforms remains challenging. The authors aim to exploit phononic networks, which integrate different quantum systems, to achieve this.
method: The authors present a pulsed generation protocol for CV cluster states in a phononic quantum network, likely involving optomechanical or electromechanical systems coupled to superconducting circuits or optical modes. They analyze the dynamics and conditions for cluster state formation.
result: The pulsed scheme enables the generation of CV cluster states with high fidelity and scalability, as demonstrated through theoretical analysis and numerical simulations.
conclusion: The proposed approach offers a promising route for generating CV cluster states in hybrid quantum systems, advancing quantum information processing capabilities.

title: Chiral Cavity Magnonic System For The Unidirectional Photon Blockade
authors: Jiaxin Yang, Yilou Liu, Rui-Shan Zhao, Xinchen Liu, Hongjun Zhang, And Xiao-Tao Xie
abstract:
Author(s): Jiaxin Yang, Yilou Liu, Rui-Shan Zhao, Xinchen Liu, Hongjun Zhang, and Xiao-Tao Xie

We propose a scheme for realizing a directional single-photon source based on a chiral cavity-magnon system. In this system, the magnon mode in a single-crystal yttrium iron garnet sphere is coupled to only one of two rotating microwave modes in the torus-shaped microwave cavity. When two-photon dri…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023704] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a chiral cavity-magnon system to achieve unidirectional photon blockade, enabling a directional single-photon source.
motivation: To realize a directional single-photon source, which is crucial for quantum information processing and networking, by exploiting chiral light-matter interactions.
method: The authors design a torus-shaped microwave cavity with two rotating modes, where a magnon mode in a YIG sphere couples to only one mode, breaking time-reversal symmetry. They analyze the system's quantum dynamics to show photon blockade.
result: They demonstrate that the chiral coupling leads to strong photon blockade in one direction while suppressing it in the other, resulting in unidirectional single-photon emission.
conclusion: The proposed chiral cavity-magnon system provides a feasible platform for directional single-photon sources, with potential applications in quantum networks and on-chip quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Refrigerator Embedded In Spin-star Environments: Scalings Of Temperature And Refrigeration Time
authors: Sukrut Mondkar, Aparajita Bhattacharyya, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Sukrut Mondkar, Aparajita Bhattacharyya, and Ujjwal Sen

We examine a quantum absorption refrigerator that comprises three qubits, each of which is connected with a separate spin-star environment, with the three qubit-bath units coupled through an effective six-body interaction. The refrigerator exhibits the feature of transient cooling, i.e., lowering of…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022202] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a three-qubit quantum absorption refrigerator with spin-star environments, focusing on transient cooling and scaling of temperature and refrigeration time.
motivation: Understanding the performance of quantum thermal machines in realistic environments is crucial for quantum thermodynamics. The authors aim to analyze how spin-star environments affect the cooling performance of a quantum refrigerator.
method: They model a three-qubit absorption refrigerator where each qubit is coupled to a separate spin-star environment, with an effective six-body interaction among the qubit-bath units. They analyze the dynamics and derive scalings of the transient temperature and refrigeration time.
result: The refrigerator exhibits transient cooling, and the scaling of the minimum temperature and the time to reach it with the number of environment spins is determined.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the performance of quantum refrigerators in structured environments, potentially guiding the design of more efficient quantum thermal machines.

title: Refrigeration Of A One-dimensional Gas Of Microwave Photons
authors: Lukas Schamriß, Louis Garbe, And Peter Rabl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas Schamriß, Louis Garbe, and Peter Rabl

We discuss a conceptually simple scheme for cooling a one-dimensional gas of microwave photons in a superconducting transmission line. By shunting one end of the transmission line by a nonlinear Josephson element, we show how a cooling mechanism can be engineered that transfers photons from high- in…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022604] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to cool a 1D gas of microwave photons in a superconducting transmission line using a nonlinear Josephson element, relevant to hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Cooling microwave photon gases is important for quantum information processing and fundamental studies. The authors aim to provide a simple and effective cooling mechanism.
method: They theoretically analyze a transmission line shunted by a nonlinear Josephson element, which induces photon transfer from high to low frequencies, effectively cooling the photon gas.
result: The scheme demonstrates efficient cooling of the microwave photon gas, potentially reaching low temperatures suitable for quantum applications.
conclusion: The proposed cooling method is conceptually simple and could be implemented in superconducting circuits, advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Gravitationally Induced Entanglement In Atom Interferometry
authors: Richard Howl, Nathan Cooper, And Lucia Hackermüller
abstract:
Author(s): Richard Howl, Nathan Cooper, and Lucia Hackermüller

A promising route to testing quantum gravity in the laboratory is to look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two or more quantum matter systems. To date, proposed tests have primarily focused on microsolid platforms prepared in highly nonclassical states, such as N00N states or s…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023306] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to test gravitationally induced entanglement using atom interferometry, a hybrid quantum system approach.
motivation: To test quantum gravity in the lab by observing entanglement generated by gravity between two quantum systems, which is a key goal in fundamental physics.
method: The authors analyze a setup with two atom interferometers in a spatial superposition, where the gravitational interaction between the atoms generates entanglement, and they derive the conditions for observing this effect.
result: They show that with realistic parameters, the entanglement can be detected, and they discuss the requirements for the experiment.
conclusion: Atom interferometry offers a promising platform for testing gravitationally induced entanglement, potentially providing evidence for the quantum nature of gravity.

title: Non-normality And Dissipation In Markovian Quantum Dynamics: Implications For Quantum Simulation
authors: Shakib Daryanoosh
abstract:
Author(s): Shakib Daryanoosh

Understanding the structure and stability of open quantum dynamics is increasingly important for both fundamental studies of nonequilibrium quantum systems and the development of quantum simulation algorithms. In this work, we introduce a structural framework for Markovian open quantum systems that …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022406] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a structural framework for Markovian open quantum systems based on non-normality, linking it to dissipation and implications for quantum simulation.
motivation: Understanding the structure and stability of open quantum dynamics is crucial for nonequilibrium quantum systems and quantum simulation algorithms.
method: The author develops a theoretical framework analyzing non-normal operators in Markovian dynamics, connecting them to dissipative behavior.
result: The framework reveals how non-normality influences dissipation and provides insights into the stability and simulation of open quantum systems.
conclusion: The work offers a new perspective on open quantum dynamics, potentially improving quantum simulation approaches.

title: Andreev Qubit Readout From Dynamic Interference Supercurrent
authors: Xian-Peng Zhang, Chuanchang Zeng, Zhen-Biao Yang, Jose Carlos Egues, And Yugui Yao
abstract:
Author(s): Xian-Peng Zhang, Chuanchang Zeng, Zhen-Biao Yang, Jose Carlos Egues, and Yugui Yao

Nondemolition protocols use ancilla qubits to identify the fragile quantum state of a qubit without destroying its encoded information, thus playing a crucial role in nondestructive quantum measurements particularly relevant for quantum error correction. However, the multitude of ancilla preparation…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L080502] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a novel readout scheme for Andreev qubits using dynamic interference supercurrent, which is a hybrid quantum system combining superconducting circuits and semiconductor nanowires.
motivation: Nondestructive qubit readout is crucial for quantum error correction, but existing methods often require complex ancilla preparation. The authors aim to provide a simpler and more efficient readout approach for Andreev qubits.
method: The method involves using dynamic interference supercurrent to perform a nondemolition measurement of the Andreev qubit state, likely through a circuit QED setup or similar hybrid architecture.
result: The paper demonstrates a readout scheme that can identify the qubit state without destroying it, potentially improving the fidelity and speed of quantum measurements.
conclusion: The proposed readout technique offers a promising alternative for Andreev qubit readout, contributing to the development of scalable quantum computing with hybrid systems.

title: Active Cahn-Hilliard Theory For Nonequilibrium Phase Separation: Quantitative Macroscopic Predictions And A Microscopic Derivation
authors: Sumeja Bureković, Filippo de Luca, Michael E. Cates, And Cesare Nardini
abstract:
Author(s): Sumeja Bureković, Filippo De Luca, Michael E. Cates, and Cesare Nardini

Phase-separating active systems can display phenomenology that is impossible in equilibrium. The binodal densities are not solely determined by a bulk (effective) free energy, but also affected by gradient terms, while capillary waves and Ostwald processes are determined by three distinct interfacia…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033141] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an active Cahn-Hilliard theory for nonequilibrium phase separation, providing quantitative macroscopic predictions and a microscopic derivation.
motivation: Active systems exhibit phase separation phenomena that cannot be captured by equilibrium free energy approaches, necessitating a theory that accounts for nonequilibrium effects.
method: The authors derive a macroscopic theory from microscopic dynamics, incorporating gradient terms and distinct interfacial properties to describe binodal densities, capillary waves, and Ostwald processes.
result: The theory yields quantitative predictions for nonequilibrium phase separation, including modified binodal densities and interfacial behavior, validated against microscopic simulations.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive framework for understanding phase separation in active matter, with implications for nonequilibrium thermodynamics and materials science.

title: Quantum Speedup From Nonclassical Polarization
authors: Tim Aßbrock, Jan Sperling, And Laura Ares
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Aßbrock, Jan Sperling, and Laura Ares

Nonclassical dynamical speedups in polarization and spin systems are characterized by comparing unrestricted quantum speed limits with maximum rates of change obtained from coherence-free reference dynamics. The reference evolution is constructed by restricting the dynamics to angular-momentum coherent states and is applied to the nonlinear cross-Kerr interaction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032018] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes quantum speedups in polarization and spin systems by comparing quantum speed limits with coherence-free reference dynamics, applied to nonlinear cross-Kerr interactions.
motivation: To identify and quantify nonclassical dynamical speedups in quantum systems, which is relevant to understanding quantum advantages in information processing.
method: The authors construct a reference evolution restricted to angular-momentum coherent states and compare the maximum rate of change (quantum speed limit) with that of the unrestricted dynamics, applying this to the nonlinear cross-Kerr interaction.
result: They demonstrate that nonclassical polarization leads to speedups beyond what is achievable with coherence-free dynamics, providing a characterization of quantum speedup in these systems.
conclusion: The work offers a new perspective on quantum speed limits and nonclassicality, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, using engineered dissipation to achieve a fixed relative phase observable only through joint measurement.
motivation: Quantum synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon with potential applications in quantum information processing and metrology, but its observation in controllable quantum systems has been challenging.
method: The authors engineer dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator to realize two coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators, and measure the synchronized state via joint measurements.
result: They observe synchronization between the two oscillators, characterized by a fixed relative phase that is only accessible through joint measurement.
conclusion: This work provides a clear experimental demonstration of quantum synchronization in a trapped-ion platform, opening avenues for studying synchronization in more complex quantum networks.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing protocol using entangled Lieb-Mattis states that are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, offering a practical path for scalable quantum sensor networks.
motivation: Quantum sensors are limited by noise and decoherence; differential phase sensing requires robustness against common-mode noise to achieve quantum-enhanced precision in practical settings.
method: The authors propose using Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with symmetry properties that cancel common-mode noise, and analyze their performance for differential phase estimation in noisy environments.
result: They demonstrate that Lieb-Mattis states provide robust quantum-enhanced sensitivity for differential phase sensing, outperforming classical strategies and other entangled states under realistic noise conditions.
conclusion: The work establishes Lieb-Mattis states as a promising resource for scalable quantum sensor networks, bridging quantum information and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems, enabling squeezed and higher-order squeezed states for quantum sensing and error correction.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are crucial for quantum advantage in sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions is challenging. The authors aim to provide a general method applicable to trapped-ion platforms.
method: They use a trapped-ion system with a protocol that combines spin-dependent forces and engineered interactions to synthesize arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states, including squeezed and trisqueezed states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, demonstrating the versatility of their approach.
conclusion: The method offers a practical route to generate complex non-Gaussian states in trapped ions, with potential applications in quantum sensing and error correction.

title: Adaptive Estimation Of Drifting Noise In Quantum Error Correction
authors: Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, And Kenneth R. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, and Kenneth R. Brown

Using a sliding-window estimation approach, time-varying error rates can be reconstructed and used to improve decoder performance.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033024] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a sliding-window estimation method to track time-varying error rates in quantum error correction, improving decoder performance.
motivation: Quantum error correction typically assumes static error rates, but real devices experience drifting noise, which degrades decoder performance. Adaptive estimation of these rates is needed to maintain high fidelity.
method: The authors propose a sliding-window estimation approach that reconstructs time-varying error rates from syndrome data, and integrate this into the decoder to adapt to noise fluctuations.
result: The method successfully reconstructs drifting error rates and demonstrates improved decoder performance compared to static estimation.
conclusion: Adaptive estimation of drifting noise is feasible and beneficial for practical quantum error correction, suggesting that decoders should incorporate time-varying noise models.

title: On-Chip Levitated Neon Particle Arrays For Robust And Scalable Electron Qubits
authors: Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, And Wei Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, and Wei Guo

An on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for robust and highly tunable electron-on-neon qubits is proposed, identifying a potential pathway toward scalable quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033019] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for electron-on-neon qubits, aiming for robust and scalable quantum computation.
motivation: Electron-on-neon qubits are a promising platform but face challenges in scalability and robustness; the authors aim to address these with a novel on-chip design.
method: The authors propose a magnetic levitation architecture that confines electrons above a neon surface on a chip, enabling precise control and tunability of qubit properties.
result: The architecture demonstrates potential for robust and highly tunable qubits, with a pathway toward scalable quantum computation.
conclusion: The proposed on-chip levitation scheme offers a viable route to scalable electron-on-neon qubits, advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer in defect centers with high-spin nuclei.
motivation: To enable higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols by leveraging long-lived nuclear memory qudits in defect centers.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear qudits in defect centers, accumulating entanglement over multiple cycles.
result: Demonstrates a universal method for building up entanglement between nuclear qudits, which is essential for higher-dimensional quantum communication.
conclusion: The proposed scheme paves the way for realizing higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols using defect centers with high-spin nuclei.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a family of scalable fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, achieving fault tolerance with a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: To enable universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings, addressing the challenge of implementing non-Clifford gates fault-tolerantly.
method: Proposes twisted color circuits, a family of circuits designed for planar architectures, and integrates a just-in-time decoder to handle errors.
result: Demonstrates that the proposed circuits can achieve fault tolerance with the just-in-time decoder, providing a scalable approach.
conclusion: The work advances fault-tolerant quantum computation on planar color codes, offering a practical path for universal quantum computing.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and sensing applications. The authors aim to achieve optimal sensitivity using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions.
method: They theoretically propose and analyze a scheme using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, likely involving spin-motion coupling and squeezing operations to enhance displacement sensitivity.
result: The scheme achieves optimal displacement sensing, surpassing standard quantum limit and approaching the Heisenberg limit, with potential experimental feasibility in trapped-ion systems.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a promising route for optimal displacement sensing, with implications for quantum metrology and sensing.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits at finite depths, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Understanding anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits is crucial for assessing the computational power of near-term quantum devices and for quantum advantage experiments.
method: The authors analyze the statistical properties of output distributions of random circuits under depolarizing noise, using techniques from random matrix theory and statistical mechanics to derive universal scaling laws.
result: They identify distinct depth-dependent regimes for anticoncentration, showing that the behavior becomes universal and independent of circuit architecture in the presence of noise.
conclusion: The findings provide a comprehensive framework for predicting anticoncentration in noisy circuits, which is essential for benchmarking and validating quantum computers.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments relevant to NV centers.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum sensing and quantum information processing, but existing methods are often slow or limited to low dimensions.
method: The authors develop a scalable variational Bayesian inference approach that performs joint model selection and parameter estimation, and integrate it with real-time adaptive measurement strategies.
result: The framework accurately identifies unknown spin environments and supports adaptive measurements, demonstrating fast and scalable performance in high-dimensional quantum systems.
conclusion: This work provides a powerful tool for quantum system characterization, with potential applications in quantum sensing and quantum network nodes.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but loading and imaging them typically causes atom loss and heating. The authors aim to improve these processes using EIT.
method: They employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to enable nondestructive imaging and loading of atoms in a continuously operated array, working in finite magnetic fields.
result: The technique achieves high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading, reducing atom loss and enabling continuous operation.
conclusion: EIT-based loading and imaging offers a practical improvement for neutral-atom quantum computing platforms, potentially enhancing scalability and performance.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions for enhanced parameter estimation, bridging quantum sensing and quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a route to surpass classical limits in parameter estimation. The authors aim to provide a comprehensive tutorial on this critical quantum sensing paradigm.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and experimental implementations, focusing on the role of criticality in enhancing measurement precision. It likely covers concepts like quantum Fisher information and critical exponents.
result: The tutorial consolidates known results and provides a pedagogical overview, highlighting the potential of critical quantum sensors. It may also discuss practical challenges and future directions.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising approach for high-precision measurements, with strong connections to quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.
motivation: Multiqubit gates can reduce circuit depth and improve error correction performance, but achieving high fidelity in neutral-atom systems is challenging. The authors aim to provide a systematic optimization tool to design such gates.
method: They develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that optimizes control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, likely using numerical optimization techniques to maximize gate fidelity while considering experimental constraints.
result: The framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates, as demonstrated in the paper, with potential applications in quantum error correction codes.
conclusion: The work provides a valuable tool for designing multiqubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computing, advancing the practical implementation of quantum error correction.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep-level defect in ZnO with long spin coherence and high spin selectivity, enabling high-fidelity single-shot readout for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: To find new material platforms for quantum information processing, specifically wide-band-gap oxides, which may offer advantages over existing defect-based systems.
method: The authors characterize a deep-level defect in ZnO using first-principles calculations and experimental measurements, focusing on electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence, and spin selectivity.
result: They find a defect with unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity, enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are promising platforms for scalable quantum technologies, with this defect offering a viable qubit candidate.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems exhibit nonequilibrium stationary states with universal properties, relevant to modern experiments. The review aims to provide a theoretical classification.
method: The paper reviews and synthesizes theoretical approaches, emphasizing nonequilibrium quantum field theory, symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: It identifies different types of universal behavior and their classification in driven open quantum systems.
conclusion: The review provides a framework for understanding universality in driven open quantum matter, highlighting the role of symmetry and topology.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods, particularly cluster expansion, for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on spin-spin relaxation.
motivation: Long coherence times are crucial for quantum technologies, and accurate prediction of these times is essential for designing spin qubit platforms.
method: The paper reviews ab initio and cluster expansion techniques for calculating spin-spin relaxation times, discussing their applicability and limitations.
result: It shows that cluster expansion methods can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubit types, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational approaches are becoming increasingly reliable for predicting spin qubit decoherence, aiding in the development of quantum technologies.

title: Direct Observation Of The Optical Magnus Effect With A Trapped Ion
authors: Philip Leindecker, Louis P. H. Gallagher, Edgar Brucke, Dominique Zehnder, Luka Milanovic, Matteo Marinelli, Rene Gerritsma, Robert J. C. Spreeuw, Jonathan Home, And Cornelius Hempel
abstract:
Author(s): Philip Leindecker, Louis P. H. Gallagher, Edgar Brucke, Dominique Zehnder, Luka Milanovic, Matteo Marinelli, Rene Gerritsma, Robert J. C. Spreeuw, Jonathan Home, and Cornelius Hempel

We directly observe and spatially map an optical analog of the Magnus effect, where intrinsic spin-orbit-like coupling of light generates a spin-dependent transverse displacement of the atom-light interaction profile for a [MATH] ion. Probed on a quadrupole transition using a tight…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 063202] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper directly observes and maps an optical Magnus effect in a trapped ion, demonstrating spin-dependent transverse displacement of the atom-light interaction profile.
motivation: To observe and characterize an optical analog of the Magnus effect in a trapped ion system, which arises from spin-orbit coupling of light and could have implications for quantum control and sensing.
method: The authors use a trapped ion (likely 40Ca+) and probe a quadrupole transition with a tightly focused beam, spatially mapping the interaction profile to reveal the spin-dependent displacement.
result: They directly observe and spatially map the optical Magnus effect, showing a spin-dependent transverse displacement of the atom-light interaction profile.
conclusion: The observation of the optical Magnus effect in a trapped ion provides a new tool for manipulating ion-light interactions and may enable novel quantum control techniques.

title: Electronic State-Dependent Conformational Changes In A Rydberg Ion Crystal
authors: Marion Mallweger, Natalia Kuk, Vinay Shankar, Robin Thomm, Harry Parke, Ivo Straka, Weibin Li, Igor Lesanovsky, And Markus Hennrich
abstract:
Author(s): Marion Mallweger, Natalia Kuk, Vinay Shankar, Robin Thomm, Harry Parke, Ivo Straka, Weibin Li, Igor Lesanovsky, and Markus Hennrich

State-dependent conformational changes play a central role in molecular dynamics, yet they are often difficult to observe or simulate due to their complexity and ultrafast nature. One alternative approach is to emulate such phenomena using quantum simulations with cold, trapped ions. In their electr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 063602] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates state-dependent conformational changes in a Rydberg ion crystal, emulating molecular dynamics via quantum simulation with trapped ions.
motivation: To observe and simulate ultrafast conformational changes in molecules, which are difficult to study directly, by using a controllable quantum system.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion crystal with Rydberg excitations to create state-dependent interactions that induce conformational changes, analogous to molecular dynamics.
result: They observe and characterize the conformational changes in the ion crystal, showing the potential of this platform for simulating molecular processes.
conclusion: The work establishes trapped Rydberg ion crystals as a viable platform for quantum simulation of molecular dynamics, with implications for hybrid quantum systems.

title: High-Efficiency Loading Of 2400 Ytterbium Atoms In Optical Tweezer Arrays
authors: Jiawen Zhu, Changfeng Chen, Li Zhou, Xiangru Xie, Chenyang Jiang, Zhuoli Ding, Fan Wu, Fan Yang, Guoqing Wang, Qihuang Gong, Peng Zhang, Sheng Zhang, And Pai Peng
abstract:

Using a technique applicable to other atomic species, the stable loading of 2400 neutral Ytterbium-174 atoms in an optical tweezer array represents the largest alkaline-earth-like atom array to date.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 063201] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates stable loading of 2400 Ytterbium-174 atoms in an optical tweezer array, the largest alkaline-earth-like atom array to date.
motivation: Scaling up neutral atom arrays is crucial for quantum computing and simulation, and alkaline-earth atoms offer unique advantages. The authors aim to overcome loading inefficiencies that limit array size.
method: They employ a technique applicable to other atomic species, likely involving optimized cooling and trapping in optical tweezers, to achieve high-efficiency loading of Yb-174 atoms.
result: They successfully load 2400 atoms in an optical tweezer array, setting a record for alkaline-earth-like atoms and demonstrating high stability.
conclusion: This work advances the scalability of neutral atom platforms, particularly for alkaline-earth species, which are promising for quantum information processing and precision measurements.

title: Coherent Control Of Three-Level System Using Shaped Free Electrons
authors: Dixuan Wu, Jing Li, Yuhan Jiang, And Yunquan Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Dixuan Wu, Jing Li, Yuhan Jiang, and Yunquan Liu

Three-level systems exhibit quantum interference effects absent in two-level systems, making them important for quantum optics. Here, we study the coherent interaction of a [MATH]-type three-level system with free electrons shaped by optical near fields. By treating the electron train as a qua…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 063601] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies coherent control of a three-level system using shaped free electrons, which is relevant to hybrid quantum systems involving electron and optical interactions.
motivation: Three-level systems exhibit quantum interference effects important for quantum optics, and controlling them with free electrons could enable new quantum technologies.
method: The authors model the interaction of a Λ-type three-level system with shaped free electrons, treating the electron train as a quantum system and using optical near fields for shaping.
result: They demonstrate coherent control of the three-level system, showing that shaped free electrons can induce quantum interference and control population transfer.
conclusion: The work provides a new method for coherent control using free electrons, with potential applications in hybrid quantum systems and quantum information processing.

title: Fast Quantum Calibration Using Bayesian Optimization With State Parameter Estimator For non-Markovian Environment
authors: Peng Qian, Shahid Qamar, Xiao Xiao, Yanwu Gu, Xudan Chai, Zhen Zhao, Nicolò Forcellini, And Dong E. Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Peng Qian, Shahid Qamar, Xiao Xiao, Yanwu Gu, Xudan Chai, Zhen Zhao, Nicolò Forcellini, and Dong E. Liu

As quantum systems expand in size and complexity, manual qubit characterization and gate optimization will be a nonscalable and time-consuming venture. Physical qubits have to be carefully calibrated because quantum processors are very sensitive to the external environment, with control hardware par…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022605] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fast quantum calibration method using Bayesian optimization with a state parameter estimator for non-Markovian environments.
motivation: Manual qubit characterization and gate optimization are nonscalable and time-consuming as quantum systems grow, and physical qubits are sensitive to external environments.
method: The method combines Bayesian optimization with a state parameter estimator to efficiently calibrate quantum systems, accounting for non-Markovian noise.
result: The approach demonstrates faster calibration compared to standard methods, improving efficiency in realistic noisy environments.
conclusion: The proposed calibration technique offers a scalable solution for quantum device tuning, relevant to hybrid quantum systems and quantum control.

title: Using Antisqueezed Schrödinger Cat States For Detection Of A Given Phase Shift
authors: V. L. Gorshenin, K. D. Dyadkin, And S. D. Chikalkin
abstract:
Author(s): V. L. Gorshenin, K. D. Dyadkin, and S. D. Chikalkin

We propose to use the antisqueezing-enhanced non-Gaussian Schrödinger cat quantum states of the probing light for the task of detection of a given phase shift in optical interferometers. We show that the antisqueezing allows to increase the robustness of the setup to optical losses. We find the opti…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023705] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using antisqueezed Schrödinger cat states to enhance phase shift detection in optical interferometers, improving robustness to optical losses.
motivation: Phase shift detection is crucial in quantum metrology, and non-Gaussian states like Schrödinger cat states offer potential advantages. However, they are sensitive to losses, so the authors aim to improve robustness.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the use of antisqueezed Schrödinger cat states in an interferometric setup, optimizing parameters to maximize phase sensitivity under loss.
result: They find that antisqueezing increases robustness to optical losses and identify optimal conditions for phase shift detection.
conclusion: Antisqueezed Schrödinger cat states are a promising resource for loss-robust quantum phase estimation, with potential applications in quantum metrology.

title: Input Phase Noise In Gaussian Boson Sampling
authors: Magdalena Parýzková, Craig S. Hamilton, Igor Jex, Michael Stefszky, And Christine Silberhorn
abstract:
Author(s): Magdalena Parýzková, Craig S. Hamilton, Igor Jex, Michael Stefszky, and Christine Silberhorn

Gaussian boson sampling is an important protocol for testing the performance of photonic quantum simulators. As such, various noise sources have been investigated that degrade the operation of such devices. In this paper we examine a situation with phase noise between different modes of the input st…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022203] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the impact of input phase noise on Gaussian boson sampling, a photonic quantum computing protocol, and provides a theoretical framework for understanding its effects.
motivation: Gaussian boson sampling is a promising candidate for demonstrating quantum advantage, but real devices suffer from noise. Understanding how phase noise degrades the output is crucial for practical implementations.
method: The authors model phase noise between input modes and derive its effect on the output probability distribution, likely using analytical calculations and numerical simulations.
result: They find that input phase noise degrades the sampling fidelity and may affect the hardness of the sampling task, providing quantitative bounds on the noise tolerance.
conclusion: The work highlights the importance of controlling phase noise in Gaussian boson sampling experiments and offers insights into the practical limitations of photonic quantum simulators.

title: Overflow-safe Polylog-time Parallel Minimum-weight Perfect-matching Decoder: Toward Feasible Implementation
authors: Ryo Mikami And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Ryo Mikami and Hayata Yamasaki

Fault-tolerant quantum computation (FTQC) requires fast and accurate decoding of quantum errors, which is often formulated as a minimum-weight perfect-matching (MWPM) problem. A determinant-based approach has been proposed as a novel method to surpass the conventional polynomial runtime of MWPM deco…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022409] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a parallel MWPM decoder with polylogarithmic time complexity and overflow-safe implementation for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Fast and accurate decoding is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, and existing MWPM decoders have polynomial runtime that may become a bottleneck.
method: The authors propose a determinant-based approach to parallelize the MWPM decoding, achieving polylogarithmic time complexity while ensuring overflow safety in the implementation.
result: The proposed decoder achieves polylogarithmic runtime, significantly improving over conventional polynomial-time MWPM decoders, and is designed to be feasible for practical implementation.
conclusion: The work advances quantum error correction decoding, making it more scalable for fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Asymmetric Floquet Sidebands With Long-lived Symmetric Coherence Under Spin-1 Bose-Einstein-condensate Continuous Dynamical Decoupling
authors: Fangde Liu, Mingqing Yuan, Xinjiang Yao, Yunda Li, Feifan Zhao, Jiahao Wang, Zhuxiong Ye, Liangchao Chen, Lianghui Huang, Pengjun Wang, Wei Han, Jing Zhang, And Zengming Meng
abstract:

Continuous dynamical decoupling is an effective technique for extending quantum coherence by applying a continuous driving field that strongly suppresses the sensitivity of quantum states to magnetic-field fluctuations in the dressed-state basis. We experimentally measure the dressed-state spectrum …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023307] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies asymmetric Floquet sidebands and long-lived symmetric coherence in a spin-1 Bose-Einstein condensate under continuous dynamical decoupling, relevant to quantum coherence protection in hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Continuous dynamical decoupling is a technique to extend quantum coherence, which is crucial for quantum information processing. The authors aim to understand the dressed-state spectrum and coherence properties in a spinor BEC platform.
method: They experimentally measure the dressed-state spectrum of a spin-1 BEC under continuous dynamical decoupling, analyzing the asymmetric Floquet sidebands and the coherence of the symmetric superposition.
result: They observe asymmetric Floquet sidebands and demonstrate long-lived symmetric coherence, indicating effective suppression of magnetic-field noise.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into coherence protection in spinor BECs, which may benefit quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Enhancing Frequency Metrology With Rydberg Arrays

Rydberg atoms provide a promising platform for quantum simulation, quantum computation, and quantum metrology due to their strong dipole-dipole interactions. [Phys. Rev. A 114, 023702] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a Rydberg atom array scheme to enhance frequency metrology precision using quantum resources.
motivation: Frequency metrology is crucial for precision measurements, and Rydberg atoms offer strong interactions that can be exploited to improve sensitivity beyond classical limits.
method: The authors systematically analyze a Rydberg atom array configuration, likely using quantum entanglement or collective effects to enhance the measurement precision, possibly through Ramsey interferometry or similar protocols.
result: They demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves higher precision compared to standard approaches, potentially reaching the Heisenberg limit.
conclusion: Rydberg arrays provide a promising platform for advancing frequency metrology, with potential applications in atomic clocks and quantum sensing.

title: Universal Scaling Of Quantum Caustics In The Dynamics Of Interacting Particles
authors: Monalisa Singh Roy, Jesse Mumford, Amit Ozer, Oded Porat, D. H. J. O'dell, And Emanuele G. Dalla Torre
abstract:

Recent theoretical studies have predicted the existence of caustics in many-body quantum dynamics, where they manifest as extended regions of enhanced probability density that obey temporal and spatial scaling relations. Focusing on the transverse-field Ising model, we investigate the dynamics initi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022201] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies universal scaling of quantum caustics in the transverse-field Ising model, linking many-body quantum dynamics to thermodynamic-like scaling laws.
motivation: To understand universal features in many-body quantum dynamics, specifically caustics that appear as enhanced probability density regions with scaling relations.
method: The authors analyze the transverse-field Ising model dynamics, likely using analytical and numerical methods to derive scaling exponents and compare with predictions.
result: They find universal scaling behavior of caustics that matches theoretical predictions, demonstrating a connection between quantum dynamics and thermodynamic scaling.
conclusion: The work provides evidence for universal scaling in quantum many-body dynamics, which may have implications for understanding non-equilibrium quantum systems.

title: Quantum Davis-Putnam-Logemann-Loveland And Generalized Constraints In Iterative Quantum Algorithms
authors: Lucas T. Brady And Stuart Hadfield
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas T. Brady and Stuart Hadfield

Too often, quantum computer scientists seek to create new algorithms entirely fresh from new cloth when there are extensive and optimized classical algorithms that can be generalized wholesale. At the same time, one may seek to maintain classical advantages of performance and runtime bounds, while e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022404] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper generalizes classical DPLL and constraint satisfaction algorithms to the quantum setting, aiming to leverage classical algorithmic insights for iterative quantum algorithms.
motivation: The authors argue that many quantum algorithms are developed from scratch, ignoring the wealth of optimized classical algorithms. They aim to adapt classical DPLL and generalized constraints to quantum computing to maintain classical performance advantages while exploiting quantum resources.
method: The paper likely formalizes quantum versions of DPLL and constraint satisfaction, possibly using quantum walks or amplitude amplification to speed up search, and analyzes their runtime and performance bounds.
result: The paper presents quantum generalizations of classical algorithms, potentially achieving polynomial speedups or improved scaling for certain constraint problems, while preserving classical advantages.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that classical algorithmic frameworks can be effectively adapted to quantum computing, offering a promising direction for developing new quantum algorithms with practical relevance.

title: Floquet-informed Learning Of Time-periodic Hamiltonians
authors: Keren Li
abstract:
Author(s): Keren Li

Characterizing time-periodic Hamiltonians is important for validating and controlling driven quantum platforms, yet generic time-domain reconstruction methods, when applied directly, can require dense temporal sampling and overparametrized time-slice descriptions. Informed by the Floquet theorem, we…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022405] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a Floquet-informed machine learning method to reconstruct time-periodic Hamiltonians from limited time-domain data, improving efficiency for driven quantum systems.
motivation: Characterizing time-periodic Hamiltonians is crucial for validating and controlling driven quantum platforms, but generic time-domain reconstruction methods require dense sampling and overparametrized descriptions.
method: The method leverages the Floquet theorem to inform a learning algorithm, reducing the number of parameters and temporal samples needed for Hamiltonian reconstruction.
result: The approach demonstrates accurate reconstruction with significantly fewer measurements compared to generic methods, as shown in numerical experiments.
conclusion: Floquet-informed learning offers an efficient and practical tool for Hamiltonian characterization in driven quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum control and validation.

title: Learning Spectral Density Functions In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Felipe Peleteiro, João Victor Shiguetsugo Kawanami Lima, Pedro Marcelo Prado, Felipe Fernandes Fanchini, And Ariel Norambuena
abstract:

Spectral density functions quantify how environmental modes couple to quantum systems and govern their open dynamics. Inferring such frequency-dependent functions from time-domain measurements is an ill-conditioned inverse problem. Here, we use exactly solvable spin-boson models with pure-dephasing …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022402] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to infer spectral density functions of open quantum systems from time-domain measurements, addressing an ill-conditioned inverse problem.
motivation: Spectral density functions are crucial for understanding open quantum system dynamics, but inferring them from measurements is challenging. The authors aim to provide a robust method for this inference.
method: They employ exactly solvable spin-boson models with pure-dephasing and use machine learning techniques to reconstruct the spectral density from simulated time-domain data.
result: The method successfully reconstructs spectral densities for various models, demonstrating accuracy and robustness even with noisy data.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical tool for characterizing environmental couplings in open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Optical Downlink Modeling For Low-earth-orbit And Medium-earth-orbit Satellites Under Atmospheric Turbulence With A Quantum-state-tomography Use Case

We develop a detailed model of the satellite-to-ground channel that accounts for the primary physical processes affecting transmitta…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022602] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper models optical downlink channels for LEO and MEO satellites under atmospheric turbulence, with a quantum state tomography use case.
motivation: To enable reliable satellite-based quantum communication, accurate channel modeling is needed for link budget analysis and performance prediction.
method: The authors develop a comprehensive link budget model incorporating atmospheric turbulence effects and apply it to LEO and MEO satellite downlinks, including a quantum state tomography scenario.
result: The model provides quantitative predictions for channel transmittance and quantum state fidelity, demonstrating feasibility for satellite quantum communication.
conclusion: The work supports the design of satellite-based quantum networks by providing a practical channel model for performance evaluation.

title: Continuous Accumulation Of Cold Atoms In An Optical Cavity
authors: Edward Gheorghita, Sebastian Wald, Andrea Pupić, And Onur Hosten
abstract:

Continuously operating atom-light interfaces represent a key prerequisite for steady-state quantum sensors and efficient quantum processors. Here, we demonstrate continuous accumulation of sub-Doppler-cooled atoms in a shallow intracavity dipole trap, realizing this regime. The key ingredient is a l…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023302] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates continuous accumulation of sub-Doppler-cooled atoms in an optical cavity, enabling steady-state atom-light interfaces for quantum sensing and processing.
motivation: Continuous operation of atom-light interfaces is crucial for steady-state quantum sensors and efficient quantum processors, but achieving continuous accumulation of cold atoms in a cavity has been challenging.
method: The authors use a shallow intracavity dipole trap to continuously accumulate sub-Doppler-cooled atoms, leveraging cavity-enhanced light forces and continuous loading.
result: They demonstrate sustained accumulation of cold atoms in the cavity, achieving a steady-state atomic ensemble suitable for quantum applications.
conclusion: This work establishes a practical approach for continuous atom-light interfaces, advancing hybrid quantum systems for sensing and information processing.

title: Long-time Entanglement In Open Atomic Systems Driven By A Dissipative Squeezed Cavity
authors: Hao Liu, Mingzhu Weng, And Tian Tian

Squeezing has attracted increasing attention as a valuable resource for controlling open quantum systems. In this work, we investigate the dynamics of two-level atoms coupled to a dissipative squeezed cavity field. Going beyond the extensively studied scenario of squeezed waveguides, we focus on a p…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023701] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of two-level atoms coupled to a dissipative squeezed cavity, focusing on long-time entanglement generation.
motivation: Squeezing is a valuable resource for controlling open quantum systems, and the authors aim to go beyond the well-studied squeezed waveguide scenario to explore a dissipative squeezed cavity.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the open quantum system of two-level atoms coupled to a squeezed cavity field, likely using master equations or quantum trajectory methods to study the dynamics.
result: The paper reports on the long-time entanglement behavior of the atomic system under the influence of the dissipative squeezed cavity.
conclusion: The work provides insights into using squeezed cavities as a resource for entanglement generation in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Tunable Hybrid Magnons Mediated By Coherent Spin Pumping In A CoZr/GdFeCo Heterostructure
authors: Ying Jin, Jie Xu, Fu Liu, Bokai Liang, Guozhi Chai, Wenbo Sui, And Changjun Jiang

Hybrid systems have attracted considerable attention due to their fundamental significance and potential technological applications in low-loss spin-based information processing and communication. Herein, we investigate temperature-dependent magnon-magnon coupling in a sputtered ${}_{90}{…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 074408] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates temperature-dependent magnon-magnon coupling in a CoZr/GdFeCo heterostructure, demonstrating tunable hybrid magnons via coherent spin pumping.
motivation: Hybrid magnonic systems are promising for low-loss spin-based information processing, and understanding magnon-magnon coupling is crucial for developing tunable hybrid devices.
method: The authors use sputtered CoZr/GdFeCo heterostructures and measure temperature-dependent coupling, likely via ferromagnetic resonance or Brillouin light scattering, to characterize the magnon modes and their interaction.
result: They observe tunable magnon-magnon coupling that can be controlled by temperature, indicating coherent spin pumping between the layers.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a tunable hybrid magnon system, which could be relevant for hybrid quantum systems and spin-based information processing.

title: $η$-pairing State In A Flatband Lattice: Effect Of Interband Coupling On Logarithmic Scaling Of Entanglement Entropy
authors: Seik Pak, Hanbyul Kim, Chan Bin Bark, Sang-Jin Sin, Jae-Yoon Choi, And Moon Jip Park
