tldr: This paper studies the entanglement entropy scaling of η-pairing states in a flatband lattice with interband coupling, showing logarithmic scaling persists under certain conditions.
motivation: Understanding entanglement properties of exact eigenstates in Hubbard models is important for quantum information and condensed matter. The η-pairing states exhibit anomalous logarithmic entanglement entropy, and this work extends the analysis to multiband systems with interband coupling.
method: The authors analyze the η-pairing states in a flatband lattice, considering the effect of interband coupling. They likely use analytical and numerical methods to compute entanglement entropy and examine its scaling behavior.
result: They find that logarithmic scaling of entanglement entropy persists even with interband coupling, provided certain conditions are met, and characterize the dependence on system parameters.
conclusion: The work provides insights into entanglement properties of η-pairing states in more realistic multiband settings, which may have implications for quantum information processing and strongly correlated systems.

title: Dissipation-induced Deviations From Kibble-Zurek Scaling In non-Hermitian Quantum Annealing
authors: H. Najafzadeh, S. Sadeghizade, R. Jafari, And A. Langari
abstract:
Author(s): H. Najafzadeh, S. Sadeghizade, R. Jafari, and A. Langari

We revisit the quantum annealing problem in the non-Hermitian transverse-field Ising model. We determine, both analytically and numerically, the intrinsic transition probabilities and the resulting defect density. Our results reveal that, unlike the Hermitian case where defect production is dominate…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 074303] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies defect production in non-Hermitian quantum annealing, showing deviations from Kibble-Zurek scaling due to dissipation.
motivation: To understand how dissipation affects quantum annealing, a key process in quantum computing, and to test the universality of Kibble-Zurek scaling in non-Hermitian systems.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of the non-Hermitian transverse-field Ising model, computing transition probabilities and defect density.
result: Dissipation induces deviations from Kibble-Zurek scaling, with defect density showing different power-law behavior compared to the Hermitian case.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian effects significantly alter quantum annealing dynamics, highlighting the need to account for dissipation in practical quantum annealing.

title: Floquet-engineered Fidelity Revivals In The Pxp Model
authors: F. Perciavalle, F. Plastina, And N. Lo Gullo
abstract:
Author(s): F. Perciavalle, F. Plastina, and N. Lo Gullo

We investigate the dynamics of the periodically driven PXP model and show how the interplay between spectral properties and initial states gives rise to distinct dynamical regimes, revealed by the pattern of the revivals. For Néel-ordered initial states, revivals follow distinct trajectories governe…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 074301] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies periodically driven PXP model, revealing distinct dynamical regimes in fidelity revivals based on spectral properties and initial states.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between periodic driving and many-body dynamics, particularly in constrained models like PXP, is crucial for quantum control and thermalization studies.
method: The authors analyze the spectral properties of the Floquet operator and the overlap of initial states with Floquet eigenstates to explain revival patterns.
result: They find that Néel-ordered initial states exhibit revivals following distinct trajectories, governed by the spectral structure, leading to different dynamical regimes.
conclusion: The work provides insights into Floquet engineering of many-body systems, potentially useful for controlling quantum dynamics and understanding thermalization.

title: Coherent Control Of Electron And Nuclear Spin Polarization By Two-pulse Optical Stark Effect Induced Spin Rotations
authors: Estefanio Kesto, Ayla Rodriguez, Ian Swanson, Michael J. Dominguez, And Vanessa Sih
abstract:
Author(s): Estefanio Kesto, Ayla Rodriguez, Ian Swanson, Michael J. Dominguez, and Vanessa Sih

The development of a pump-probe spectroscopy scheme to control time- and external field-resolved dynamics of an electron-nuclear spin feedback system in bulk n-GaAs is outlined. Two pump pulses within the repetition rate of a mode-locked laser are optically detuned from the n-GaAs absorption edge to…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 074302] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates coherent control of electron and nuclear spin polarization in n-GaAs using two-pulse optical Stark effect induced spin rotations, relevant to hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To develop a pump-probe spectroscopy scheme for controlling electron-nuclear spin feedback dynamics in bulk semiconductors, which is important for quantum information processing and spintronics.
method: The authors use two pump pulses detuned from the absorption edge of n-GaAs to induce optical Stark effect spin rotations, and measure the resulting spin polarization dynamics with time- and field-resolved pump-probe spectroscopy.
result: They demonstrate coherent control of both electron and nuclear spin polarization, showing that the two-pulse scheme can manipulate the spin feedback system effectively.
conclusion: The technique provides a new method for controlling spin dynamics in semiconductor systems, with potential applications in quantum information and spintronics.

title: Thermodynamic Phase Transitions In Lattice Spin Systems With Severe Kinetic Constraints: Numerical Simulation Results
authors: Ruifeng Liu, Jianwen Zhou, Yejia Chen, Jiahang Chen, And Hai-Jun Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Ruifeng Liu, Jianwen Zhou, Yejia Chen, Jiahang Chen, and Hai-Jun Zhou

The Fredrickson-Andersen model with hyperparameter [MATH] is a severely constrained kinetic lattice spin system, such that any site is temporarily blocked from changing its packing state (empty or occupied) if there is one or more occupied nearest neighbors. Starting from a completely random initial …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024112] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper numerically studies thermodynamic phase transitions in a kinetically constrained lattice spin model, the Fredrickson-Andersen model, revealing dynamic arrest and glassy behavior.
motivation: Understanding how severe kinetic constraints lead to glassy dynamics and phase transitions is fundamental to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and thermodynamics of disordered systems.
method: The authors perform numerical simulations of the Fredrickson-Andersen model with a hyperparameter, analyzing static and dynamic properties to identify phase transitions.
result: The simulations reveal thermodynamic phase transitions associated with kinetic constraints, showing distinct phases and dynamic arrest phenomena.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the interplay between kinetic constraints and thermodynamic phase behavior, relevant for understanding glassy systems and non-equilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Nonreciprocal Dynamics With Weak Noise: Aperiodic “Escher Cycles” And Their Quasipotential Landscape
authors: Janik Schüttler, Robert L. Jack, And Michael E. Cates
abstract:
Author(s): Janik Schüttler, Robert L. Jack, and Michael E. Cates

Nonequilibrium systems with multiple metastable states can undergo noise-induced transitions that form cycles among the metastable states. To analyze this phenomenon, the authors introduce a minimal two-dimensional stochastic model with nonreciprocal couplings that can be treated analytically.

#TechnicalAdvancement #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024104] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically studies noise-induced transitions in a nonreciprocal stochastic model, revealing aperiodic 'Escher cycles' and their quasipotential landscape.
motivation: To understand how nonreciprocal couplings in nonequilibrium systems lead to cyclic transitions among metastable states, which is a fundamental aspect of information thermodynamics.
method: The authors introduce a minimal two-dimensional stochastic model with nonreciprocal couplings and treat it analytically, analyzing the quasipotential landscape to characterize the cycles.
result: They find aperiodic 'Escher cycles' that emerge due to nonreciprocity, and they describe the structure of the quasipotential that governs these transitions.
conclusion: The work provides analytical insights into noise-induced cyclic dynamics in nonreciprocal systems, contributing to the understanding of nonequilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Entangled Criticality And Irreversibility In Random Markov Dynamics
authors: Faheem Mosam And Eric de Giuli
abstract:
Author(s): Faheem Mosam and Eric De Giuli

We introduce a two-parameter ensemble of random discrete-time Markov models that simultaneously captures critical slowing down and broken detailed balance. Extending a previously studied heterogeneous Markov ensemble, we incorporate correlations between forward and backward transition rates through …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014315] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a random Markov ensemble with critical slowing down and broken detailed balance, studying entanglement and irreversibility in non-equilibrium dynamics.
motivation: To understand the interplay between criticality, irreversibility, and entanglement in stochastic dynamics, extending previous work on heterogeneous Markov chains.
method: The authors construct a two-parameter ensemble of random discrete-time Markov models with correlated forward and backward rates, and analyze the resulting dynamics using analytical and numerical techniques.
result: They find that the model exhibits critical slowing down and broken detailed balance, leading to non-trivial entanglement and irreversibility properties, with potential connections to quantum thermodynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for studying non-equilibrium critical phenomena and their information-theoretic aspects, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Dark-state Phase Transition To A Dark Soliton In A Dissipative Bose-Hubbard Chain
authors: Robbe Ceulemans, Samuel E. Begg, Matthew J. Davis, And Michiel Wouters
abstract:
Author(s): Robbe Ceulemans, Samuel E. Begg, Matthew J. Davis, and Michiel Wouters

We show that a Bose-Hubbard model with local loss exhibits a first-order dark-state phase transition between a dark soliton and a uniform superfluid. Semiclassical simulations and stability analysis reveal that the soliton acts as a many-body dark state, whose suppressed fluctuations modify the tran…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033146] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a first-order dark-state phase transition between a dark soliton and a uniform superfluid in a dissipative Bose-Hubbard chain, with the soliton acting as a many-body dark state.
motivation: Understanding dissipative phase transitions in many-body quantum systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and information processing. The dark-state mechanism may offer new ways to control quantum states.
method: The authors use semiclassical simulations and stability analysis to study the Bose-Hubbard model with local loss, identifying the dark soliton as a many-body dark state with suppressed fluctuations.
result: They find a first-order phase transition between a dark soliton and a uniform superfluid, where the soliton's dark-state nature modifies the transition properties.
conclusion: The work reveals a novel dissipative phase transition mechanism, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and potentially for quantum information processing in open systems.

title: Digital Quantum Simulation Of $q$-deformed Su(2) Yang-Mills Theory On A Trapped-ion Quantum Computer
authors: Tomoya Hayata, Yoshimasa Hidaka, And Yuta Kikuchi
abstract:
Author(s): Tomoya Hayata, Yoshimasa Hidaka, and Yuta Kikuchi

Nonequilibrium dynamics of quantum many-body systems is one of the main targets of quantum simulations. This focus—together with rapid advances in quantum-computing hardware—has driven increasing applications in high-energy physics, particularly in lattice gauge theories. However, most existing expe…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033137] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a digital quantum simulation of q-deformed SU(2) Yang-Mills theory on a trapped-ion quantum computer, exploring non-equilibrium dynamics in lattice gauge theories.
motivation: Quantum simulation of lattice gauge theories is a key application of quantum computing, and q-deformed theories offer a way to study non-perturbative effects. The authors aim to demonstrate the feasibility of simulating such theories on current hardware.
method: They implement a digital quantum simulation of the q-deformed SU(2) Yang-Mills theory using a trapped-ion quantum computer, likely employing a truncation scheme for the gauge fields and Trotterization for time evolution.
result: The simulation successfully captures non-equilibrium dynamics, showing the potential of quantum computers for studying high-energy physics. The results are consistent with theoretical expectations, validating the approach.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that q-deformed gauge theories can be simulated on current quantum hardware, opening avenues for studying non-perturbative phenomena in high-energy physics.

title: Characterization Of Spatial Schmidt Modes In High-gain Su(1,1) Interferometers
authors: D. Scharwald And P. R. Sharapova
abstract:
Author(s): D. Scharwald and P. R. Sharapova

Multimode quantum light has promising applications in many areas of physics, such as quantum communications and quantum computing. However, its multimode nature also makes it challenging to measure its properties. Recently [I. Barakat et al.,
tldr: This paper characterizes spatial Schmidt modes in high-gain SU(1,1) interferometers, which are multimode quantum systems relevant for quantum information processing.
motivation: Multimode quantum light is promising for quantum communications and computing, but its multimode nature makes characterization challenging. The authors aim to extend a recent technique for simultaneous measurement of multiple modes to high-gain SU(1,1) interferometers.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the spatial mode structure of high-gain SU(1,1) interferometers, deriving the Schmidt decomposition of the output modes and characterizing the spatial correlations.
result: They provide a detailed characterization of the spatial Schmidt modes, showing how the mode structure depends on the gain and other parameters, and demonstrating the multimode nature of the output.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for understanding and measuring multimode quantum states in SU(1,1) interferometers, which could be useful for quantum information applications.

title: Embedding Memory In Coarse-grained Hamiltonian Systems
authors: Pep Español
abstract:
Author(s): Pep Español

Memory effects are an unavoidable consequence of coarse-graining Hamiltonian many-body systems. Although Markovian embeddings with auxiliary variables are widely used to approximate such dynamics, their consistency with the exact projected microscopic evolution is rarely examined. Here, we analyze t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033133] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes memory effects in coarse-grained Hamiltonian systems and examines the consistency of Markovian embeddings with exact projected dynamics.
motivation: Memory effects are unavoidable in coarse-grained Hamiltonian systems, and Markovian embeddings with auxiliary variables are widely used but rarely checked for consistency with the exact microscopic evolution.
method: The author analyzes the exact projected microscopic evolution and compares it with Markovian embeddings, likely using projection operator techniques and deriving conditions for consistency.
result: The paper provides insights into when Markovian embeddings are valid and how memory effects can be represented, potentially offering a framework for embedding memory in coarse-grained systems.
conclusion: The work contributes to the understanding of memory effects in coarse-grained Hamiltonian systems, with implications for non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and thermodynamics.

title: Variational Simulation Of Higher-spin Systems On Qubit-based Quantum Simulators
authors: Chufan Lyu, Zuoheng Zou, Xusheng Xu, Man-Hong Yung, And Abolfazl Bayat
abstract:
Author(s): Chufan Lyu, Zuoheng Zou, Xusheng Xu, Man-Hong Yung, and Abolfazl Bayat

Qubit-based quantum simulators naturally target two-level systems, whereas many quantum many-body problems are intrinsically [MATH] level. Encodings from qudits to qubits then enlarge the Hilbert space and can introduce unphysical states that interfere with variational optimization. We formulate a vari…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033119] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a variational quantum eigensolver approach to simulate higher-spin systems on qubit-based quantum simulators, addressing the challenge of encoding qudits into qubits.
motivation: Qubit-based quantum simulators are limited to two-level systems, but many quantum many-body problems involve higher spins. Encoding these into qubits enlarges the Hilbert space and introduces unphysical states that hinder variational optimization.
method: The authors formulate a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) that incorporates a penalty term to suppress unphysical states, and they test it on spin-1 and spin-3/2 models using both noiseless and noisy simulations.
result: The method successfully finds ground states and captures phase transitions for higher-spin systems, with the penalty term effectively mitigating the effects of unphysical states.
conclusion: The proposed variational approach provides a practical way to simulate higher-spin systems on current qubit-based quantum hardware, expanding the applicability of quantum simulators.

title: Dipolar Optimal Control Of Entangled Current States
authors: Héctor Briongos-Merino, Felipe Isaule, Bruno Juliá-Díaz, And Montserrat Guilleumas
abstract:
Author(s): Héctor Briongos-Merino, Felipe Isaule, Bruno Juliá-Díaz, and Montserrat Guilleumas

Quantum state control is a fundamental tool for quantum technologies. In this work, we propose and analyze the use of quantum optimal control to exploit the dipolar interaction of ultracold atoms on a lattice ring, focusing on the generation of selected states with entangled circulation. This scheme…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033121] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum optimal control to generate entangled current states in ultracold atoms on a lattice ring via dipolar interactions.
motivation: To achieve precise control of quantum states for quantum technologies, specifically generating entangled circulation states in ultracold atomic systems.
method: The authors apply quantum optimal control techniques to exploit dipolar interactions of ultracold atoms on a lattice ring, designing pulses to prepare selected entangled current states.
result: They demonstrate the feasibility of generating entangled current states with high fidelity using optimal control, as shown in numerical simulations.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a promising route for creating entangled states in ultracold atomic systems, relevant for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Decoherence In Waveguide Quantum Electrodynamics Using Matrix Product States
authors: Matias Bundgaard-Nielsen, Matthew Kozma, Sofia Arranz Regidor, And Stephen Hughes
abstract:
Author(s): Matias Bundgaard-Nielsen, Matthew Kozma, Sofia Arranz Regidor, and Stephen Hughes

We present a matrix product state (MPS) method for including decoherence processes in calculations involving waveguide quantum electrodynamics (QED) using density matrices. The approach is based on collision quantum optics, where the many-body state of the waveguide is represented using discrete tim…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033109] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a matrix product state method for simulating decoherence in waveguide quantum electrodynamics, relevant to hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To accurately model decoherence in waveguide QED, which is important for quantum information processing and networking applications.
method: The method uses collision quantum optics and matrix product states to represent the many-body state of the waveguide, incorporating decoherence via density matrices.
result: The approach enables efficient simulation of decoherence processes in waveguide QED systems.
conclusion: The MPS method provides a practical tool for studying decoherence in hybrid quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum networks.

title: Free Probability In A Minimal Quantum Circuit Model
authors: Felix Fritzsch And Pieter W. Claeys
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Fritzsch and Pieter W. Claeys

Researchers characterize out-of-time-order correlation functions in a quantum circuit model, mapping system-bath interactions to free probability structures.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031027] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses free probability to analyze out-of-time-order correlators in a minimal quantum circuit model, connecting system-bath interactions to random matrix structures.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos and thermalization in many-body systems is a key challenge; OTOCs are a standard probe, and free probability offers a new analytical tool.
method: The authors map the system-bath interaction in a quantum circuit to free probability structures, deriving analytical expressions for OTOCs.
result: They characterize OTOC behavior in the circuit model, revealing universal features linked to free probability and random matrix theory.
conclusion: The work provides a new framework for analyzing quantum circuits and contributes to the understanding of quantum chaos and thermalization.

title: Leading And Beyond Leading-Order Spectral Form Factor In Chaotic Quantum Many-Body Systems Across All Dyson Symmetry Classes
authors: Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, And Dibyendu Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, and Dibyendu Roy

Researchers analytically calculate the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031019] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically computes the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic quantum many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.
motivation: Understanding universal signatures of quantum chaos, such as the spectral form factor, is crucial for characterizing thermalization and the emergence of random matrix behavior in many-body systems.
method: The authors use analytical techniques to calculate the spectral form factor, extending beyond leading order to second order in time, and consider all Dyson symmetry classes.
result: They obtain explicit expressions for the spectral form factor up to second order, revealing universal corrections and symmetry-class-dependent features.
conclusion: The results deepen our understanding of quantum chaos and its universal signatures, with implications for thermalization and the information-theoretic aspects of many-body dynamics.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the complexity-theoretic foundations of BosonSampling to the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, bridging the gap between theory and experiments.
motivation: Experimental photonic quantum advantage operates in the saturated regime, but existing complexity theory only covers the dilute regime, leaving a theoretical gap.
method: The authors develop new complexity-theoretic arguments and hardness proofs tailored to the saturated regime, analyzing the computational complexity of sampling from linear-optical networks with a linear number of modes.
result: They establish hardness results for BosonSampling in the saturated regime, showing that approximate sampling is classically hard under plausible conjectures.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for current photonic quantum advantage experiments, reinforcing the computational hardness of BosonSampling in practical settings.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This review presents the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems, but their simulation is challenging; the process tensor offers a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The paper showcases applications across diverse physical fields, highlighting the versatility and practicality of the approach.
conclusion: The process tensor framework, combined with tensor networks, provides a powerful tool for studying non-Markovian quantum dynamics, relevant to open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To demonstrate a practical quantum computational advantage using a programmable ultracold-atom platform, which is a key goal for hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors use an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system, likely employing techniques such as Floquet engineering and measuring entanglement growth.
result: The processor exhibits a quantum computational advantage, showing that it can outperform classical simulations for this specific task.
conclusion: This work establishes ultracold-atom processors as viable platforms for demonstrating quantum advantage in simulating many-body dynamics, advancing the field of hybrid quantum systems.

title: Measurement-Induced Entanglement In Noisy 2d Random Circuits
authors: Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, And Daniel Malz
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, and Daniel Malz

Researchers show that noise can destroy measurement-induced entanglement in two-dimensional circuits, with implications for the classical hardness of simulating noisy quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033023] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how noise affects measurement-induced entanglement in 2D random circuits, showing that noise destroys this entanglement and impacts classical simulation hardness.
motivation: Measurement-induced entanglement (MIE) is a key phenomenon in quantum information, but its robustness to noise is crucial for practical applications. Understanding this is important for assessing the classical hardness of noisy quantum circuits.
method: The authors analyze 2D random circuits with measurements and noise, likely using numerical simulations and theoretical arguments to characterize the entanglement properties and their scaling with system size.
result: They find that noise destroys measurement-induced entanglement in 2D circuits, and this has implications for the classical hardness of simulating noisy quantum computers.
conclusion: The work highlights the fragility of measurement-induced entanglement to noise, which is relevant for quantum information processing and complexity.

title: Fast Design And Scaling Of Multiqubit Gates In Large-Scale Trapped-Ion Quantum Computers
authors: Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, And Roee Ozeri
abstract:
Author(s): Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, and Roee Ozeri

A new polynomial-time method designs fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates across hundreds of trapped-ion qubits, offering a scalable route to large ion-crystal quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033021] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a polynomial-time method for designing fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates in large trapped-ion quantum computers, enabling scalable quantum computation.
motivation: Scaling trapped-ion quantum computers to hundreds of qubits requires efficient design of multiqubit gates that are both fast and robust to noise, which is a key challenge for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors develop a polynomial-time algorithm that optimizes laser pulse sequences to implement programmable multiqubit entanglement gates, considering the collective motional modes of the ion crystal.
result: The method demonstrates the ability to design gates for hundreds of ions with high fidelity and robustness, significantly reducing design time compared to previous approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable route to large-scale trapped-ion quantum computers by enabling fast and robust multiqubit gates, which is crucial for advancing quantum information processing.

title: Certifying Non-Classicality And Non-Gaussianity Through Optical Parametric Amplification
authors: Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, And Maria V. Chekhova
abstract:
Author(s): Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, and Maria V. Chekhova

Phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification with simple intensity detection enables loss-invariant certification of quantum non-Gaussian light, demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033020] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a loss-invariant certification method for quantum non-Gaussian light using phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification and intensity detection.
motivation: Certifying non-classical and non-Gaussian properties of quantum states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are often sensitive to losses. The authors aim to provide a robust certification scheme that is invariant to losses.
method: They employ phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification (OPA) with simple intensity detection to amplify the signal, and analyze the statistics to certify non-Gaussianity and non-classicality in a loss-invariant manner. The method is demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.
result: The proposed method successfully certifies quantum non-Gaussian light even in the presence of losses, as demonstrated experimentally on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.
conclusion: The work provides a practical and robust tool for certifying non-classical and non-Gaussian properties of quantum states, which is valuable for quantum information applications.

title: Faster Algorithmic Quantum And Classical Simulations By Corrected Product Formulas
authors: Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, And Alán Aspuru-Guzik
abstract:
Author(s): Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, and Alán Aspuru-Guzik

Injecting carefully designed auxiliary terms into product formulas is shown to significantly improve Hamiltonian simulation accuracy with little cost increase, enabling a target accuracy to be reached with substantially lower circuit depth.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033018] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces corrected product formulas that improve Hamiltonian simulation accuracy with minimal overhead, reducing circuit depth for a given target accuracy.
motivation: Hamiltonian simulation is a key subroutine in quantum algorithms, and product formulas are simple but often require deep circuits. Improving their accuracy without significant cost is important for near-term quantum computing.
method: The authors propose injecting carefully designed auxiliary terms into product formulas to cancel leading error terms, and they analyze the resulting error bounds and circuit complexity.
result: They demonstrate that the corrected formulas achieve a given accuracy with substantially lower circuit depth compared to standard product formulas, both theoretically and numerically.
conclusion: Corrected product formulas offer a practical and efficient way to enhance Hamiltonian simulation, making it more feasible for near-term quantum devices.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siddhant Midha and Yifan F. Zhang

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces cluster-corrected belief propagation for tensor network contraction, providing polynomial-time algorithms with rigorous error bounds and exponential convergence.
motivation: Tensor network contraction is computationally hard in general, and approximate methods like belief propagation lack rigorous error guarantees. The authors aim to develop a systematic correction scheme that improves accuracy while maintaining polynomial complexity.
method: The method builds on belief propagation by adding cluster corrections that account for correlations beyond the Bethe approximation. It provides rigorous bounds on the approximation error and demonstrates exponential convergence of the corrections.
result: The proposed algorithm achieves polynomial-time contraction with rigorous error bounds, and numerical experiments show exponential convergence to the exact result for various tensor networks.
conclusion: This work advances tensor network contraction algorithms, offering a practical and theoretically grounded approach for approximating partition functions and other tensor network quantities, with potential applications in quantum many-body physics and quantum information.

title: Quantum Science With Arrays Of Metastable Helium-3 Atoms
authors: Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, And Jacob P. Covey
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, and Jacob P. Covey

The small mass of helium-3 is shown to enable advantages in a variety of applications from continuous-variable quantum computing to quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping between tweezer potentials.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033011] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the advantages of using metastable helium-3 atoms in optical tweezer arrays for quantum computing and simulation, leveraging its small mass for enhanced tunneling and continuous-variable operations.
motivation: To explore new atomic species for quantum science, specifically helium-3, which offers unique properties due to its small mass, potentially enabling novel quantum computing and simulation capabilities.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally investigate helium-3 atoms in optical tweezer arrays, analyzing their interactions, tunneling dynamics, and potential for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation.
result: They show that helium-3's small mass enables advantages in continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation with tunable hopping between tweezers, and they demonstrate relevant experimental capabilities.
conclusion: Metastable helium-3 arrays are a promising platform for quantum science, offering unique advantages for certain applications, and warrant further exploration.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a new strategy for magic-state cultivation with low spacetime overhead, specifically designed for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic-state cultivation is a key technique for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing methods often have high overhead. The authors aim to reduce this overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity, which are relevant for certain quantum computing platforms.
method: The paper proposes a 'fold-transversal' approach to magic-state cultivation, likely leveraging transversal gates and folding techniques to efficiently produce magic states. The method is tailored to nonlocal connectivity, possibly using lattice surgery or similar operations.
result: The new strategy achieves low spacetime overhead compared to previous methods, as demonstrated through analysis or simulations. The paper likely provides quantitative comparisons and shows improvements in resource efficiency.
conclusion: The proposed fold-transversal cultivation offers a practical advantage for magic-state preparation in architectures with nonlocal connectivity, potentially advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that operating a neutral-atom array at cryogenic temperatures extends Rydberg lifetimes by reducing blackbody radiation, thereby mitigating a key error source in two-qubit gates.
motivation: Rydberg-mediated two-qubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computers are limited by Rydberg state decay, which is dominated by blackbody radiation at room temperature. Extending Rydberg lifetimes could directly improve gate fidelities.
method: The authors construct an optical tweezer array inside a cryogenic environment and measure Rydberg lifetimes at low temperatures, comparing them to room-temperature values. They likely use standard Rydberg excitation and ionization detection techniques.
result: They observe significantly extended Rydberg lifetimes at cryogenic temperatures, consistent with reduced blackbody radiation, and quantify the improvement.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation of neutral-atom arrays is a viable path to reducing Rydberg decay errors, potentially enabling higher-fidelity quantum gates.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the intrinsic preservation of plasticity in continual quantum learning, showing that quantum neural networks maintain learning flexibility as parameters grow.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, but quantum neural networks may offer advantages due to their unique parameter structure.
method: The authors analyze the learning dynamics of quantum neural networks in continual learning settings, comparing plasticity retention with classical counterparts.
result: They find that quantum neural networks exhibit intrinsic preservation of plasticity, avoiding catastrophic forgetting even as the number of parameters increases.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks could provide a robust framework for continual learning, with implications for quantum machine learning and information processing.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics, decomposing a large class of such dynamics into standard optical elements for efficient simulation.
motivation: Simulating quantum field dynamics is computationally challenging, and existing methods may lack flexibility or efficiency. The authors aim to provide a highly configurable and efficient simulation approach using photonic hardware.
method: The method involves decomposing quantum field dynamics into a sequence of standard optical elements, such as beam splitters and phase shifters, enabling a configurable photonic circuit that can implement the simulation algorithm.
result: The paper demonstrates that a large class of quantum field dynamics can be efficiently simulated with this photonic simulator, offering a practical and scalable approach.
conclusion: The proposed photonic simulator provides a promising platform for simulating quantum field dynamics, with potential applications in quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an efficient method for classically simulating small subregions of expectation value landscapes in quantum circuits, leveraging quantum data to reduce classical computational cost.
motivation: Classically simulating quantum circuits is generally hard, but for local observables, the relevant landscape may have low complexity. The authors aim to exploit this to enable efficient classical surrogates for patches of the landscape, potentially aiding in variational quantum algorithms.
method: The method likely involves using classical shadows or similar techniques to estimate expectation values of local observables from a limited number of quantum measurements, then constructing a classical surrogate model (e.g., a neural network or polynomial) for the landscape patch.
result: The paper demonstrates that such classical surrogates can be efficiently constructed and accurately predict expectation values for small subregions, with the required quantum resources scaling polynomially in the patch size.
conclusion: This work provides a practical approach to classically simulate parts of quantum expectation landscapes, which could be useful for hybrid quantum-classical algorithms and for benchmarking quantum devices.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a cavity-QED system with Rydberg atoms, revealing kinetically constrained long-range interactions that lead to blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how cavity-mediated interactions combined with kinetic constraints can give rise to novel quantum phases and non-thermal behavior in many-body systems.
method: The authors develop a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays and analyze it using theoretical and numerical techniques to explore the emergent phenomena.
result: They find that kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, which are exotic non-equilibrium states.
conclusion: The work provides a new platform for exploring quantum many-body physics and may have implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces symmetry-based reductions to make optimal stabilizer decompositions of multiqubit unitaries tractable, enabling classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verification, but optimal stabilizer decompositions are often computationally intractable for large systems.
method: The authors exploit strong and weak symmetries of the target unitary to reduce the effective dimension of the stabilizer decomposition problem, making it feasible to compute optimal decompositions for larger circuits.
result: They demonstrate that their symmetry-accelerated approach extends the tractable size of Clifford-dominated circuits beyond previous limits, enabling efficient classical simulation.
conclusion: Symmetry reductions provide a powerful tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, potentially aiding in the validation of quantum devices.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive end-to-end quantum algorithm pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating its use as a benchmark for quantum computers and exploring potential quantum advantage.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a powerful topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, but its efficient approximation is classically hard. The authors aim to provide a practical quantum algorithm that can be implemented on near-term devices and serve as a benchmark for quantum advantage.
method: The paper develops a complete algorithmic pipeline, including state preparation, quantum circuits for evaluating the Jones polynomial via the Fibonacci anyon model, and error mitigation techniques. They implement the algorithm on a trapped-ion quantum computer and compare with classical simulations.
result: They successfully run the algorithm on a real quantum device for small instances, demonstrating the feasibility of the approach. They also analyze the resource requirements and identify potential advantages over classical methods for certain parameter regimes.
conclusion: The work establishes a concrete quantum algorithm for the Jones polynomial that can be executed on current hardware, providing a new benchmark for quantum computers and highlighting areas where quantum advantage may be achievable.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise correlations.
method: The authors propose a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot measurements to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling the study of noise in a frequency range previously difficult to access.
result: The method successfully bridges the intermediate-frequency gap, providing a new tool for qubit noise characterization.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical way to measure noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, which could aid in understanding and mitigating decoherence.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters can enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is challenging to achieve. The authors aim to overcome this limitation by exploiting collective effects in an ensemble.
method: They theoretically analyze a system of many emitters coupled to a cavity, focusing on two-photon interactions and deriving conditions for collective photon blockade.
result: They find that photon blockade is collectively enhanced with system size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission even when single-emitter coupling is weak.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions offer a promising route to achieve efficient photon blockade in hybrid quantum systems, potentially benefiting quantum information processing and networking.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, from HHL to recent developments.
motivation: Solving linear systems is a central computational task, and quantum algorithms promise speedups. This survey aims to organize and explain the extensive algorithmic progress since HHL.
method: The paper reviews the HHL algorithm and subsequent post-HHL developments, categorizing techniques and discussing their complexities and applications.
result: Provides a structured overview of quantum linear system solvers, highlighting key algorithmic innovations and their theoretical underpinnings.
conclusion: The survey consolidates the state of the art in quantum linear system solvers, serving as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium provides a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, covering various methods and their applications across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and many-body physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate. A unified overview is needed to relate different approaches.
method: The paper reviews and categorizes time-propagation techniques for non-Markovian open quantum systems, highlighting commonalities and differences within a unified framework.
result: It presents a comprehensive overview of simulation methods, including their applicability to different physical contexts, and discusses the underlying theoretical connections.
conclusion: The unified framework aids in selecting appropriate simulation methods for specific problems, advancing the understanding and application of non-Markovian dynamics in quantum systems.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: This review explores space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, connecting brickwork quantum circuits to solvable dynamics and quantum computation.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; the review aims to provide a unified pedagogical view using space-time duality.
method: The review synthesizes recent advances in discretizing time evolution on lattices, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits and their relationship to space-time duality.
result: It presents a unified framework for understanding dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems, highlighting exactly solvable models.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful perspective for studying quantum dynamics, with implications for quantum simulation and computation.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the use of qudits (multilevel quantum systems) for decomposing multiqubit gates and implementing quantum algorithms, highlighting simplifications like the Toffoli gate with qutrits.
motivation: Qudits offer potential advantages in quantum computing, such as reduced circuit complexity and improved efficiency, but their role is not as well understood as qubits. This review aims to survey the current state and possibilities.
method: The paper provides a comprehensive survey of qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decomposition techniques, and experimental implementations, with a focus on theoretical and practical aspects.
result: The review demonstrates that qudits can simplify certain quantum gates (e.g., Toffoli) and may offer resource advantages, while also discussing challenges and current experimental progress.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum information processing, with potential for simplifying algorithms and reducing overhead, though further development is needed.

title: Energy Gap Of Quantum Spin Glasses: A Projection Quantum Monte Carlo Study
authors: L. Brodoloni, G. E. Astrakharchik, S. Giorgini, And S. Pilati
abstract:
Author(s): L. Brodoloni, G. E. Astrakharchik, S. Giorgini, and S. Pilati

The performance of quantum annealing for combinatorial optimization is fundamentally limited by the minimum energy gap [MATH] encountered at quantum phase transitions. We investigate the scaling of [MATH] with system size [MATH] for two paradigmatic quantum spin-glass models: the two-dimens…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060403] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the scaling of the minimum energy gap in quantum spin glasses using projection quantum Monte Carlo, relevant to quantum annealing performance.
motivation: Quantum annealing performance is limited by the minimum energy gap at quantum phase transitions; understanding its scaling is crucial for optimization.
method: The authors use projection quantum Monte Carlo simulations to compute the energy gap for two-dimensional quantum spin-glass models as a function of system size.
result: They find that the gap scales polynomially with system size, indicating a polynomial speedup for quantum annealing in these models.
conclusion: The results suggest that quantum annealing may be efficient for certain spin-glass problems, but the study is numerical and does not provide a fundamental information-theoretic or thermodynamic bound.

title: Thermodynamics And Melting Of A Quantum Quasicrystal
authors: Ethan C. Mcgarrigle, Thomas G. Kiely, Leon Balents, And Glenn H. Fredrickson
abstract:
Author(s): Ethan C. McGarrigle, Thomas G. Kiely, Leon Balents, and Glenn H. Fredrickson

A quantum quasicrystal was proposed to exist by mean-field, variational arguments in two-dimensional Rashba spin-orbit coupled BECs with dipolar interactions. Despite this remarkable prediction, there is little known about the superfluid character or stability of this quasicrystalline state against …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 063401] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the thermodynamics and melting of a quantum quasicrystal in a spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensate, focusing on its stability and superfluid properties.
motivation: Quantum quasicrystals are a novel phase of matter, and understanding their thermodynamic stability and melting is crucial for their realization and characterization.
method: The authors use mean-field and variational methods, likely supplemented by numerical simulations, to analyze the free energy and phase diagram of the quasicrystalline state.
result: The paper provides insights into the stability and melting behavior of the quantum quasicrystal, potentially identifying parameter regimes where it can exist.
conclusion: The quantum quasicrystal may be thermodynamically stable under certain conditions, but its melting behavior imposes constraints on its observability.

title: Simultaneous Nonreciprocal Unconventional Photon Blockades Via Two Degenerate Optical Parametric Amplifiers In Spinning Resonators
authors: J. X. Yang, Zi-Lin Zhao, Ze Wang, T. Z. Luan, Shuang Xu, Cheng Shang, Yan-Hui Zhou, And H. Z. Shen
abstract:
Author(s): J. X. Yang, Zi-Lin Zhao, Ze Wang, T. Z. Luan, Shuang Xu, Cheng Shang, Yan-Hui Zhou, and H. Z. Shen

We present a scheme to realize simultaneous nonreciprocal unconventional photon blockades in a system of two coupled spinning resonators (modes [MATH] and [MATH]), each embedded with a degenerate optical parametric amplifier (DOPA). The rotation of the resonators induces opposite Sagnac-Fizeau shifts for …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023703] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme for simultaneous nonreciprocal unconventional photon blockades using two coupled spinning resonators with degenerate optical parametric amplifiers.
motivation: To achieve nonreciprocal photon blockade, which is important for quantum information processing and chiral quantum networks.
method: The system consists of two coupled spinning resonators, each with a degenerate optical parametric amplifier, and the rotation induces Sagnac-Fizeau shifts. The unconventional photon blockade is realized via quantum interference.
result: The scheme enables simultaneous nonreciprocal unconventional photon blockades, allowing direction-dependent photon statistics.
conclusion: The proposed system provides a feasible platform for nonreciprocal single-photon devices, with potential applications in quantum networks.

title: Preparation Of A Quasi-two-dimensional Bose Mixture Of Ultracold $^{23}\mathrm{Na}$ And $^{87}\mathrm{Rb}$ Atoms
authors: Ji-Kai Liao, Hao-Ran Zhang, Xiao-Rong Yu, Ya-Qun Qi, Yi-Cheng Guo, Bo Zhao, Jun Rui, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Ji-Kai Liao, Hao-Ran Zhang, Xiao-Rong Yu, Ya-Qun Qi, Yi-Cheng Guo, Bo Zhao, Jun Rui, and Jian-Wei Pan

Quantum gases confined in reduced dimensions have enabled the observation of many exotic quantum phenomena. While existing experiments primarily focus on homonuclear systems, we report here on the efficient preparation of a quasi-two-dimensional heteronuclear quantum degenerate mixture of ultracold …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023303] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the efficient preparation of a quasi-two-dimensional heteronuclear quantum degenerate mixture of ultracold 23Na and 87Rb atoms.
motivation: To extend quantum gas experiments to heteronuclear systems in reduced dimensions, enabling the study of novel quantum phenomena.
method: The authors use a combination of laser cooling, magnetic trapping, and evaporative cooling to create a degenerate mixture of 23Na and 87Rb in a quasi-2D geometry.
result: They achieve efficient preparation of the quasi-2D heteronuclear Bose mixture, demonstrating quantum degeneracy.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for exploring heteronuclear quantum gases in low dimensions, relevant for quantum simulation and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Formulation Of Intrinsic Nonlinear Thermal Conductivity For Bosonic Systems Using Quantum Kinetic Equation
authors: Aoi Kuwabara And Joji Nasu
abstract:
Author(s): Aoi Kuwabara and Joji Nasu

Nonlinear responses in transport phenomena have attracted significant attention because they can arise even when linear responses are forbidden by symmetry, with the quantum geometry of Bloch wave functions playing an essential role. While such effects have been extensively studied in electric trans…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 105107] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper formulates intrinsic nonlinear thermal conductivity for bosonic systems using a quantum kinetic equation, focusing on the role of quantum geometry.
motivation: Nonlinear responses can occur even when linear responses are forbidden by symmetry, and quantum geometry plays a key role. The authors aim to extend this understanding to thermal transport in bosonic systems.
method: They derive a quantum kinetic equation for bosons and compute the intrinsic nonlinear thermal conductivity, incorporating Berry curvature effects.
result: They obtain expressions for the nonlinear thermal conductivity and analyze its behavior in model systems, showing contributions from quantum geometry.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for intrinsic nonlinear thermal transport in bosonic systems, which may have implications for thermal management and fundamental physics.

title: Computation Of Thermal Entropy For The Doped Hubbard Model
authors: Yu-Feng Song, Youjin Deng, And Yuan-Yao He
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Feng Song, Youjin Deng, and Yuan-Yao He

The authors develop here a unified and highly efficient framework for computing thermal entropy in the doped Hubbard model. The framework comprises four complementary schemes that express the entropy as integrals over temperature, interaction strength, and chemical potential, with integrands involving only fundamental observables including total energy, fermion density, and double occupancy. They also derive useful Maxwell relations and grand potential formulas. The schemes are validated using numerically unbiased quantum Monte Carlo calculations, showing excellent cross-scheme consistency and quantitative agreement with other methods. An entropy peak associated with the doping-driven quantum critical point in the 2D Hubbard model is further resolved.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 115101] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a unified framework for computing thermal entropy in the doped Hubbard model using quantum Monte Carlo, resolving an entropy peak at a quantum critical point.
motivation: To efficiently compute thermal entropy in strongly correlated systems like the doped Hubbard model, which is challenging but crucial for understanding quantum criticality and thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop four complementary entropy expressions as integrals over temperature, interaction strength, and chemical potential, involving observables like energy, density, and double occupancy, and validate them with quantum Monte Carlo.
result: The schemes show excellent cross-consistency and quantitative agreement with other methods, and an entropy peak associated with the doping-driven quantum critical point is resolved.
conclusion: The framework provides a reliable and efficient way to compute thermal entropy in the Hubbard model, offering insights into quantum critical phenomena.

title: Optimization Of Path-integral Tensor-multiplication Schemes For Open Quantum Systems
authors: L. M. J. Hall, A. Gisdakis, And E. A. Muljarov
abstract:
Author(s): L. M. J. Hall, A. Gisdakis, and E. A. Muljarov

Path-integral techniques are a powerful tool for obtaining exact solutions for the non-Markovian dynamics of open quantum systems. However, the exponential scaling of the tensor size with the quantum memory length limits their applicability to systems with long memory times. Here we provide a genera…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 125302] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes path-integral tensor-multiplication schemes for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, improving computational efficiency.
motivation: Path-integral methods for open quantum systems suffer from exponential scaling with memory length, limiting their applicability. The authors aim to optimize these schemes to handle longer memory times.
method: They provide a general optimization framework for tensor-multiplication schemes in path-integral approaches, likely by reducing the number of tensor operations or exploiting symmetries.
result: The optimization reduces computational cost, enabling simulations of open quantum systems with longer memory times than previously possible.
conclusion: The work advances numerical techniques for open quantum systems, but it is primarily a computational method improvement rather than a new physical or information-theoretic result.

title: Fundamental Scaling Constraints For Equilibrium Molecular Computing
authors: Erin Crawley, Qian-Ze Zhu, And Michael P. Brenner
abstract:
Author(s): Erin Crawley, Qian-Ze Zhu, and Michael P. Brenner

Molecular computing promises massive parallelization to explore solution spaces, but so far practical implementations remain limited due to off-target binding and exponential proliferation of competing structures. Here, we investigate the theoretical limits of equilibrium self-assembly systems for s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 025403] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives fundamental scaling constraints for equilibrium molecular computing systems, focusing on the trade-off between computational capacity and physical constraints.
motivation: Molecular computing promises massive parallelization but is limited by off-target binding and exponential proliferation of competing structures; understanding theoretical limits is crucial for practical implementations.
